classes.lower_bound: The true figure is at least this.
classes.modelled_range: An estimate built on stated assumptions.

figures.how: Every race he has a result in, across seven series. Heats are not counted.
figures.label: Races

figures.how: Races where he was classified first.
figures.label: Wins

figures.how: Races where he finished in the top three.
figures.label: Podiums

figures.how: Races where he finished tenth or better.
figures.label: Top tens

figures.caveat: Daytona counts his 142 laps, not the 780 the shared car ran.
figures.how: His laps in every race added up. At Daytona only the laps he drove himself count.
figures.label: Race laps

figures.caveat: About 29% of one trip around the equator.
figures.how: Each race's laps times that track's length, added up race by race.
figures.label: Miles raced

figures.caveat: The turn counts come from each track's published layout; an oval counts as four corners.
figures.how: His laps in each race times the number of numbered turns on that track.
figures.label: Corners in races

figures.caveat: Covers 122 of 150 races and includes time behind the safety car.
figures.how: The official race time from the start to his finish, added up over the races that publish one.
figures.label: Time racing, timed races

figures.caveat: Covers 148 of 150 races; the other 2 had no laps. Real laps are slower than his best, so the true time is longer.
figures.how: The timed races, plus his laps times his best lap for the races with no official time.
figures.label: Time racing, all races

figures.caveat: Leaves out sessions with no lap count and every private test.
figures.how: Race time, plus his laps times his best lap in every practice, qualifying and test session with a lap count.
figures.label: Time on track, all official sessions

figures.caveat: Some names appear twice under different spellings, so this is between 491 and 498 people. About half are from the one 24-hour race at Daytona.
figures.how: Every other driver name on the results of the races he was in, counted once each.
figures.label: Other drivers in his races

figures.caveat: Between 261 and 268 people, for the same reason.
figures.how: The same count without the Daytona 24-hour race, so only the drivers he raced in single-seaters.
figures.label: Other drivers, leaving out Daytona

figures.how: Different circuits he has raced at. Two layouts at one circuit count once.
figures.label: Tracks

figures.how: Countries those circuits are in.
figures.label: Countries

figures.caveat: The least distance anyone could cover between his races, not his real travel: trips home and testing are left out.
figures.how: A straight line from each race's track to the next race's track, added up in date order.
figures.label: Miles between tracks

figures.caveat: The stretch factors are assumptions. Still only track to track, not his real travel.
figures.how: The straight lines stretched to allow for roads on short trips and flight paths on long ones.
figures.label: Miles between tracks, by road and air

figures.caveat: Out of the 2,699 days from his first race meeting to his last.
figures.how: Every day from the first to the last day of each race meeting, counting a day once even when two meetings share it.
figures.label: Days at race meetings

figures.caveat: 4 sessions have no date and are left out.
figures.how: Different dates on which he ran in at least one official session.
figures.label: Days he was on track

figures.how: Calendar weeks, Monday to Sunday, that held at least one day of a race meeting.
figures.label: Weeks with a race meeting

figures.caveat: The fuel rates are assumptions, not measurements.
figures.how: His race miles times a low, middle and high guess at how much fuel each car uses per mile.
figures.label: Fuel burned in races

figures.caveat: The fuel rates are assumptions, and sessions with no lap count are left out.
figures.how: The same fuel rates applied to his miles in every practice, qualifying, test and race.
figures.label: Fuel burned in all official sessions

figures.caveat: Being named does not mean he caused it. Only INDY NXT publishes these reports.
figures.how: Safety-car periods in his races where the official report names his car.
figures.label: Cautions he was named in

figures.how: INDY NXT races where the official result says he stopped before the finish, and why.
figures.label: Races he retired from

figures.caveat: All three were for avoidable contact. Other series' penalties are not in the data.
figures.how: Penalties the INDY NXT stewards gave him in races.
figures.label: Penalties

figures.how: His age on September 6, 2026, the day of his latest race.
figures.label: Age at his latest race

figures.how: Every day from his birth to September 6, 2026, counting both.
figures.label: Days alive

figures.how: His days at race meetings out of every day he has been alive.
figures.label: Days at race meetings, share of his life

figures.how: His days at race meetings out of every day from his first race meeting to his last.
figures.label: Days at race meetings, share of his racing years

figures.how: Days he ran in at least one official session, out of every day he has been alive.
figures.label: Days on track, share of his life

figures.how: Days he ran in at least one official session, out of every day from his first race meeting to his last.
figures.label: Days on track, share of his racing years

figures.how: Calendar weeks, Monday to Sunday, from the week he was born to the week of September 6, 2026.
figures.label: Weeks lived

figures.how: Weeks that held at least one day of a race meeting, out of every week he has lived.
figures.label: Race weeks among the weeks he has lived

travelLegs.how: Each leg is a straight line from one race meeting's track to the next one's, in date order. Drive or flight is a rule of thumb (same country and under 750 miles counts as a drive), not how he travelled.
